can_answer: partly: the file can show annual pedestrian injury counts in Brooklyn crashes, but has no pedestrian, walking-trip, or traffic exposure denominator to measure individual risk or establish overall road safety
metric: Annual number of pedestrians injured, calculated as the sum of number_of_pedestrians_injured
denominator: None; a count, not a rate
population: Pedestrian injuries recorded in police-reported crash rows with borough Brooklyn
filters: retain rows with number_of_pedestrians_injured present for the sum
years: Complete calendar years 2013-2025; exclude 2026 because the file ends June 11, 2026
data_check_findings_and_decisions: The check showed that 2026 is partial (the latest crash_date is 2026-06-11), so the period was revised to complete years 2013-2025. In 2013-2025, borough is NULL on 659,713 city rows (30.9% of 2,132,218 rows); those rows cannot be assigned to Brooklyn and are excluded under the borough filter. There are no empty, placeholder, or unrecognized borough values; Brooklyn is stored as BROOKLYN. No Brooklyn rows have missing dates or common default dates 1900-01-01/1970-01-01. The pedestrian injury field has zero missing values in Brooklyn plan-year rows; retain all eligible rows.
limitations: Police-reported crash records lack pedestrian, walking-trip, or traffic exposure denominators, so these are absolute pedestrian injury counts, not individual risk rates; borough is NULL on 659,713 city crash rows (30.9% of 2,132,218) in 2013-2025 and these are excluded from the Brooklyn filter, and 2026 is partial and omitted.
